title: Exact exponential moments of interval quasi-stationary laws for Lévy processes, and the saturation of idealised QSD restart
shortTitle: Restart from a quasi-stationary law: the exact constant and the real budget scale
oneLine: A conjecture of Garcia, Bermolen, Jonckheere and Shneer on restart-based rare-event simulation holds up to a constant, but the constant is not one (0.850 in their own example), and idealised quasi-stationary restart saturates at budgets of order exp(ηL), far below the range stated in their restart theorem.
abstract: Restarting a simulation from a quasi-stationary distribution (QSD) is a simple way to look for a rare high level L of a process that drifts away from it, for example in rare-event simulation or in exploration for model-free simulation and reinforcement learning. Its efficiency is governed by an exponential moment of the QSD on the interval (0, L), and Garcia, Bermolen, Jonckheere and Shneer (Stochastic Systems, 2026) conjectured that this moment grows like exp((λ*−η)L), noting that this is exact for Brownian motion. For Lévy processes with a Gaussian component and jumps of either sign, this candidate proves that every exponential moment of the interval QSD has an exact limit after normalisation, with constants written through the ladder-height exponents of the Esscher-centred process; the core input is an exact L⁻² asymptotic for the two boundary layers of the centred QSD. The conjecture therefore holds on the logarithmic scale and up to constants, but its ratio-one reading fails: the constant is below one for every spectrally negative process with jumps, above one for every spectrally positive one, and 0.85014864899… in the source's own example (certified by interval arithmetic). For idealised QSD restart the success rate is asymptotic to R* exp(−ηL) with explicit R*, and the curve 1 − exp(−R* B exp(−ηL)) is accurate uniformly in the budget B in relative error, so the linear budget regime of the source's restart theorem is B = O(exp(ηL)), not B = o(exp(λ*L)). The moment theorem is extended to spectrally negative processes without a Gaussian part, and the first-order finite-L corrections are identified in the source model. AI-assisted, unrefereed candidate; no external peer review, independent reproduction or formal verification is claimed.

keyResults: Exact moments (Theorem 2.2, proof): for a Lévy process with a Gaussian component, jumps of either sign and a Cramér root λ*, every exponential moment M_L(θ) of the QSD on (0, L) has an exact normalised limit: bounded for θ < η (recovering Kyprianou and Palmowski's half-line formula), of order L² at θ = η, and ∼ C(θ) exp((θ−η)L) for θ > η, with C(θ) given by ladder-height exponents of the Esscher-centred process.

The engine (Theorem 2.3, proof): the centred QSD is a sine-shaped bulk with two thin boundary layers whose masses are exactly of order L⁻²; the left layer follows the ascending ladder renewal function, the right one the descending ladder. The conjecture's constant is C* = K_r(λ*−η)/K_ℓ(η) = G₊(λ*−η)/G₋(η).

The ratio-one reading fails (Proposition 2.9, proof; certified enclosure): C* = 1 for Brownian motion, C* < 1 for every spectrally negative process with jumps, C* > 1 for every spectrally positive one, and C* = 0.85014864899… in the source's own example.

Restart saturates at exp(ηL) (Theorem 2.6 and Corollary 2.7, proof): the success rate of idealised QSD restart is r_L ∼ R* exp(−ηL), the curve 1 − exp(−R* B exp(−ηL)) has relative error at most |a_L − 1| at every budget, and the linear regime of the source's restart theorem is B = O(exp(ηL)), not B = o(exp(λ*L)); an exact Brownian example refutes the wider range.

Extensions: spectrally negative processes without a Gaussian part, C* = η²ψ″(η)/(2κ∞) ≤ 1 (Theorem 8.1, proof under a scale-function positivity condition); in the source model the killing rate sees an effective length L + δ₊ + δ₋ and both constants carry relative error π²(δ₋ − δ₊)/(2L) ≈ 0.497/L (Theorems 9.1–9.2, proof given standard QSD-density regularity).

narration: When restarting a simulation pays off, and when it stops paying. An Evidence Press briefing. Some of the most important events in a model are rare: a queue overflowing, a reserve running out, a learning agent finally reaching a distant goal. Simulating them directly is wasteful, because almost every run drifts away and fails. One simple remedy is restart. Whenever a run falls below a floor, throw it away and start again, not from the beginning, but from a point drawn from the quasi-stationary distribution. That is the pattern the process settles into when it is watched only on the occasions it has survived between the floor and the target for a long time. In a 2026 paper in Stochastic Systems, Garcia, Bermolen, Jonckheere and Shneer showed that the waiting time for success under this scheme is exactly exponential, and that its rate depends on one number: an exponential average over the quasi-stationary distribution. They conjectured how fast that number grows as the target moves further away, noting that the guess is exact for Brownian motion. This release computes the number exactly for a broad class of random processes with jumps. The growth rate they predicted is right, but the hoped-for constant of one is not. In their own example the constant is about 0.85. It is below one whenever all the jumps point downwards and above one whenever they all point upwards. The reason is that the quasi-stationary distribution has a smooth sine-shaped middle and two very thin layers at its edges, and those layers set the constant. The practical consequence concerns the simulation budget. Restart's chance of success grows in proportion to the budget only up to a definite scale, after which extra simulation buys almost nothing. That scale is much smaller than the range stated in the original restart theorem, and the release gives a corrected range and an explicit budget rule. The results assume perfect, free draws from the quasi-stationary distribution, which real particle methods only approximate. This is an anonymous, AI-assisted, unrefereed candidate, not peer reviewed or independently reproduced. Published on 21 October 2026, its paper and evidence are linked from the Evidence Press release page. This briefing uses an AI-generated voice and is not additional scientific evidence.

decisionObject.description: A resolution of the Garcia–Bermolen–Jonckheere–Shneer conjecture on exponential moments of interval QSDs for Lévy processes with a Gaussian component (true up to an explicit constant, false in its ratio-one reading), with the exact restart constant and a corrected budget range for their restart theorem.
decisionObject.scope: Real Lévy processes with a Gaussian component, a finite cumulant near the Cramér root and continuous monitoring; spectrally negative processes also without a Gaussian part. Idealised restart with exact, free QSD draws; no claim for random walks, two-sided pure-jump processes or implementable Fleming–Viot restart.
